items.title: Le dimanche, Central appartient aux travailleuses
items.dek: À Hong Kong, des centaines de milliers de femmes venues d'Asie du Sud-Est vivent chez leurs employeurs. Leur seul jour libre, elles prennent la rue.
paragraphs: Le dimanche matin, à Hong Kong, le quartier d'affaires de Central change de visage. Sous les tours des banques, sur les passerelles et dans les passages couverts, des milliers de femmes s'installent sur des cartons ou des nattes. Elles partagent des plats, se coupent les cheveux, chantent, prient ou jouent aux cartes. Beaucoup viennent des Philippines ; d'autres se retrouvent plutôt à Causeway Bay, autour du parc Victoria, où l'on entend souvent parler indonésien.

Ces femmes sont des travailleuses domestiques étrangères. Hong Kong en compte plus de 300 000, venues surtout des Philippines et d'Indonésie. Elles font le ménage, la cuisine et les courses, et elles s'occupent des enfants ou des personnes âgées. Les règles de l'immigration les obligent à vivre chez leur employeur : pendant six jours, elles habitent donc sur leur lieu de travail, souvent dans un espace minuscule. Le dimanche, leur jour de repos, la rue devient leur salon.

Combien gagnent-elles ? Le gouvernement fixe pour elles un salaire minimum spécial. Depuis le 3 octobre 2026, il est de 5 220 dollars de Hong Kong par mois, soit environ 665 dollars américains : une hausse de 2,35 %, après 5 100 dollars l'année précédente. L'indemnité de nourriture, versée quand l'employeur ne fournit pas les repas, n'a pas bougé depuis 2023 : au moins 1 236 dollars par mois. Ces travailleuses ne profitent pas du salaire minimum horaire de la ville, et aucune loi ne limite le nombre d'heures qu'elles font chaque jour.

Leur séjour dépend aussi de leur contrat. Quand celui-ci se termine, elles ont en général deux semaines pour trouver un nouvel employeur ou pour quitter Hong Kong. Une employée qui se plaint risque donc de perdre à la fois son travail, son logement et son droit de rester. Pour cette raison, les associations de travailleuses migrantes demandent depuis longtemps la fin de l'obligation de vivre chez l'employeur et une limite au temps de travail.

Le gouvernement explique qu'il cherche un équilibre entre les besoins des travailleuses et ce que les familles peuvent payer. Mais le dimanche à Central raconte une autre histoire, selon de nombreux observateurs : celle d'une ville riche qui ne fonctionne pas sans ces femmes, et qui leur laisse pourtant si peu de place qu'elles doivent en inventer une, chaque semaine, sur le trottoir.
paragraphs_en: On Sunday mornings in Hong Kong, the Central business district changes its face. Beneath the bank towers, on the footbridges and in the covered walkways, thousands of women settle down on cardboard sheets or mats. They share food, cut each other's hair, sing, pray or play cards. Many come from the Philippines; others gather instead in Causeway Bay, around Victoria Park, where Indonesian is often heard.

These women are foreign domestic workers. Hong Kong has more than 300,000 of them, mostly from the Philippines and Indonesia. They clean, cook and shop, and they look after children or elderly people. Immigration rules require them to live with their employer: for six days, they therefore live at their workplace, often in a tiny space. On Sunday, their day off, the street becomes their living room.

How much do they earn? The government sets a special minimum wage for them. Since 3 October 2026 it has been 5,220 Hong Kong dollars a month, about 665 US dollars: a rise of 2.35%, after 5,100 dollars the previous year. The food allowance, paid when the employer does not provide meals, has not changed since 2023: at least 1,236 dollars a month. These workers are not covered by the city's hourly minimum wage, and no law limits the number of hours they work each day.

Their stay also depends on their contract. When it ends, they generally have two weeks to find a new employer or to leave Hong Kong. A worker who complains therefore risks losing her job, her housing and her right to stay all at once. For this reason, migrant workers' associations have long demanded an end to the live-in requirement and a limit on working time.

The government says it seeks a balance between the workers' needs and what families can afford. But Sundays in Central tell another story, according to many observers: that of a rich city that cannot function without these women, yet leaves them so little room that they must invent some, every week, on the pavement.
paragraphs_de: Sonntagmorgens verändert das Geschäftsviertel Central in Hongkong sein Gesicht. Unter den Bankentürmen, auf Fußgängerbrücken und in überdachten Passagen lassen sich Tausende Frauen auf Kartons oder Matten nieder. Sie teilen Essen, schneiden einander die Haare, singen, beten oder spielen Karten. Viele kommen von den Philippinen; andere treffen sich eher in Causeway Bay rund um den Victoria Park, wo man oft Indonesisch hört.

Diese Frauen sind ausländische Hausangestellte. Hongkong zählt mehr als 300 000 von ihnen, vor allem von den Philippinen und aus Indonesien. Sie putzen, kochen und kaufen ein und kümmern sich um Kinder oder alte Menschen. Die Einwanderungsregeln verpflichten sie, bei ihrem Arbeitgeber zu wohnen: Sechs Tage lang leben sie also an ihrem Arbeitsplatz, oft auf winzigem Raum. Am Sonntag, ihrem Ruhetag, wird die Straße zu ihrem Wohnzimmer.

Wie viel verdienen sie? Die Regierung legt für sie einen eigenen Mindestlohn fest. Seit dem 3. Oktober 2026 beträgt er 5 220 Hongkong-Dollar im Monat, etwa 665 US-Dollar: ein Plus von 2,35 % nach 5 100 Dollar im Vorjahr. Das Verpflegungsgeld, das gezahlt wird, wenn der Arbeitgeber kein Essen stellt, ist seit 2023 unverändert: mindestens 1 236 Dollar im Monat. Für diese Arbeiterinnen gilt der stündliche Mindestlohn der Stadt nicht, und kein Gesetz begrenzt, wie viele Stunden sie täglich arbeiten.

Ihr Aufenthalt hängt auch von ihrem Vertrag ab. Endet er, haben sie in der Regel zwei Wochen Zeit, um einen neuen Arbeitgeber zu finden oder Hongkong zu verlassen. Eine Angestellte, die sich beschwert, riskiert also, auf einen Schlag Arbeit, Unterkunft und Aufenthaltsrecht zu verlieren. Deshalb fordern Organisationen von Migrantinnen seit Langem das Ende der Wohnpflicht beim Arbeitgeber und eine Begrenzung der Arbeitszeit.

Die Regierung erklärt, sie suche einen Ausgleich zwischen den Bedürfnissen der Arbeiterinnen und dem, was Familien bezahlen können. Doch der Sonntag in Central erzählt nach Ansicht vieler Beobachter eine andere Geschichte: die einer reichen Stadt, die ohne diese Frauen nicht funktioniert und ihnen dennoch so wenig Platz lässt, dass sie sich jede Woche selbst einen schaffen müssen – auf dem Gehsteig.

items.grammar: The pronoun « en » replaces a noun introduced by a quantity: « Hong Kong en compte plus de 300 000 » means 'Hong Kong has more than 300,000 of them' (en = des travailleuses domestiques). The number stays after the verb, while « en » goes before it. The same pronoun appears at the end of the text: « elles doivent en inventer une » ('they must invent one [a place]'); with an infinitive, « en » sits directly in front of that infinitive.
items.grammar_de: Das Pronomen « en » ersetzt ein Nomen nach einer Mengenangabe: « Hong Kong en compte plus de 300 000 » heißt „Hongkong zählt mehr als 300 000 davon“ (en = des travailleuses domestiques). Die Zahl bleibt hinter dem Verb, « en » steht davor. Am Ende des Textes taucht es wieder auf: « elles doivent en inventer une » („sie müssen sich einen [Platz] schaffen“); bei einem Infinitiv steht « en » direkt vor dem Infinitiv.

items.title: Carinhoso: uma canção de amor com duas partes
items.dek: Um choro de 1917, uma letra de 1936 e uma gravação de 1937.
paragraphs: "Carinhoso" é uma música muito famosa no Brasil. É um choro. O compositor é Pixinguinha. Ele nasce no dia 23 de abril de 1897.
Pixinguinha escreve a música por volta de 1917. Ele tem só 20 anos. Mas ele não mostra a música a ninguém. Por quê? Porque, naquela época, um choro tem três partes. "Carinhoso" tem só duas.
Nos anos 1920, a música tem uma gravação sem letra, só com instrumentos. Um crítico não gosta. Para ele, o começo parece um foxtrote americano.
Em 1936, a cantora Heloísa Helena precisa de uma música nova. Ela pede ajuda ao amigo Braguinha. Ele escreve a letra de "Carinhoso" em uma noite.
No dia 28 de maio de 1937, o cantor Orlando Silva grava a canção. É a música mais tocada do ano de 1937!
Hoje, "Carinhoso" tem mais de 200 gravações. Elis Regina, Paulinho da Viola e Marisa Monte cantam a música. Muitas pessoas chamam a canção de "segundo hino nacional".
Como é a música? É uma canção de amor, simples e doce. E o dia 23 de abril, aniversário de Pixinguinha, é o Dia Nacional do Choro.
paragraphs_en: "Carinhoso" is a very famous song in Brazil. It is a choro. The composer is Pixinguinha. He is born on 23 April 1897.
Pixinguinha writes the music around 1917. He is only 20 years old. But he doesn't show the music to anyone. Why? Because at that time a choro has three parts. "Carinhoso" has only two.
In the 1920s the music gets a recording without lyrics, only with instruments. A critic doesn't like it. For him, the beginning sounds like an American foxtrot.
In 1936 the singer Heloísa Helena needs a new song. She asks her friend Braguinha for help. He writes the lyrics of "Carinhoso" in one night.
On 28 May 1937 the singer Orlando Silva records the song. It is the most played song of 1937!
Today "Carinhoso" has more than 200 recordings. Elis Regina, Paulinho da Viola and Marisa Monte sing it. Many people call the song the "second national anthem".
What is the song like? It is a love song, simple and sweet. And 23 April, Pixinguinha's birthday, is National Choro Day.
paragraphs_zh: 《Carinhoso》是巴西一首非常有名的乐曲。它是一首肖罗（choro）。作曲者是皮欣吉尼亚。他生于1897年4月23日。
皮欣吉尼亚大约在1917年写下这首曲子。他那时才20岁。但他没有把曲子给任何人看。为什么？因为在那个年代，一首肖罗要有三个部分，而《Carinhoso》只有两个。
20世纪20年代，这首曲子有了一个没有歌词、只有乐器的录音。一位评论家不喜欢它。他觉得开头像一首美国狐步舞曲。
1936年，女歌手埃洛伊莎·埃莱娜需要一首新歌。她请朋友布拉吉尼亚帮忙。他用一个晚上写好了《Carinhoso》的歌词。
1937年5月28日，歌手奥兰多·席尔瓦录下了这首歌。它是1937年播放最多的歌！
今天，《Carinhoso》有两百多个录音版本。埃利斯·雷吉娜、保利尼奥·达维奥拉和玛丽莎·蒙特都唱过它。很多人把这首歌叫作“第二国歌”。
这首歌是什么样的？它是一首情歌，简单又甜美。而4月23日，皮欣吉尼亚的生日，是全国肖罗日。
items.grammar: Three spellings, one sound: "Por que…?" starts a question (Why…?), "Por quê?" with an accent stands at the end or alone ("Why?"), and "porque" in one word means "because". In the text: "Por quê? Porque, naquela época, um choro tem três partes."
items.grammar_zh: 三种写法，同一个读音：“Por que…?” 放在问句开头（为什么……？）；带重音符号的 “Por quê?” 放在句末或单独使用（“为什么？”）；连写的 “porque” 意思是“因为”。文中：“Por quê? Porque, naquela época, um choro tem três partes.”

items.title: Carinhoso: o choro que passou anos na gaveta
items.dek: Como uma peça que o próprio Pixinguinha achava "incompleta" virou o segundo hino nacional do Brasil.
paragraphs: Toda família brasileira tem uma música que aparece sem ser convidada: no aniversário da avó, no fim de uma roda de samba, no violão do tio que só sabe quatro acordes. Em muitas casas, essa música é "Carinhoso". Quase todo mundo reconhece a melodia nos primeiros compassos; pouca gente sabe que ela passou anos esquecida numa gaveta, porque o próprio autor tinha vergonha dela.

O autor era Alfredo da Rocha Vianna Júnior, o Pixinguinha, nascido em 23 de abril de 1897 e considerado por muitos o grande organizador da música popular brasileira. Por volta de 1917 — a data exata ainda é discutida pelos pesquisadores —, com uns vinte anos, ele compôs um choro diferente. O problema era a forma: a peça tinha só duas partes, e os choros da época deveriam ter três. Décadas depois, num depoimento ao Museu da Imagem e do Som do Rio, Pixinguinha contou que foi por isso que a guardou.

Quando enfim saiu da gaveta, "Carinhoso" ganhou uma gravação instrumental nos anos 1920 — e não agradou a todos. O crítico Cruz Cordeiro, da revista Phonoarte, achou que a introdução lembrava um foxtrote, e chegou-se a falar na "jazzificação" de Pixinguinha. Hoje a história soa irônica: justamente o que parecia estrangeiro demais virou símbolo do que há de mais brasileiro.

A virada veio em 1936. A cantora Heloísa Helena precisava de uma música nova para um espetáculo beneficente no Theatro Municipal do Rio de Janeiro e pediu socorro ao amigo Braguinha, também conhecido como João de Barro. Ele não tinha nada pronto, mas se ofereceu para escrever versos para aquela melodia antiga. Segundo o próprio Braguinha, a letra ficou pronta em uma noite — e o pagamento foi uma gravata italiana.

Em 28 de maio de 1937, Orlando Silva, um dos cantores mais populares do rádio, gravou a canção pela Victor, e "Carinhoso" foi a música mais tocada daquele ano. Desde então, foram mais de duzentas gravações, de Dalva de Oliveira e Elizeth Cardoso a Elis Regina, Paulinho da Viola e Marisa Monte; em 1950, houve até uma versão em inglês para o cinema. Não é à toa que muita gente a chama de "segundo hino nacional".

Ao ouvir, preste atenção à melodia, que sobe e desce com uma delicadeza quase de conversa, e ao contraste entre as duas partes — justamente aquelas que pareceram poucas ao jovem compositor. A letra de Braguinha fala de um amor terno, de um coração que se alegra só de ver a pessoa amada. E, se você precisar de uma desculpa para escutá-la de novo, lembre-se: 23 de abril, aniversário de Pixinguinha, é o Dia Nacional do Choro.
paragraphs_en: Every Brazilian family has a song that shows up uninvited: at grandma's birthday, at the end of a samba circle, on the guitar of the uncle who only knows four chords. In many homes that song is "Carinhoso". Almost everyone recognises the melody in the first bars; few people know that it spent years forgotten in a drawer, because its own author was ashamed of it.

The author was Alfredo da Rocha Vianna Júnior, known as Pixinguinha, born on 23 April 1897 and considered by many the great organiser of Brazilian popular music. Around 1917 — researchers still debate the exact date — at about twenty, he composed an unusual choro. The problem was its form: the piece had only two parts, and choros of the time were supposed to have three. Decades later, in a testimony to Rio's Museum of Image and Sound, Pixinguinha said that this was why he put it away.

When it finally left the drawer, "Carinhoso" got an instrumental recording in the 1920s — and not everyone liked it. The critic Cruz Cordeiro, of the magazine Phonoarte, felt the introduction resembled a foxtrot, and people even spoke of Pixinguinha's "jazzification". Today the story sounds ironic: the very thing that seemed too foreign became a symbol of all that is most Brazilian.

The turning point came in 1936. The singer Heloísa Helena needed a new song for a charity show at the Theatro Municipal in Rio de Janeiro and turned for help to her friend Braguinha, also known as João de Barro. He had nothing ready, but offered to write words for that old melody. According to Braguinha himself, the lyrics were done in one night — and his payment was an Italian tie.

On 28 May 1937 Orlando Silva, one of the most popular radio singers, recorded the song for Victor, and "Carinhoso" was the most played song of that year. Since then there have been more than two hundred recordings, from Dalva de Oliveira and Elizeth Cardoso to Elis Regina, Paulinho da Viola and Marisa Monte; in 1950 there was even an English version for the cinema. No wonder many people call it the "second national anthem".

When you listen, pay attention to the melody, which rises and falls with an almost conversational delicacy, and to the contrast between the two parts — the very ones that seemed too few to the young composer. Braguinha's lyrics speak of a tender love, of a heart that rejoices just at the sight of the beloved. And if you need an excuse to hear it again, remember: 23 April, Pixinguinha's birthday, is National Choro Day.
paragraphs_zh: 每个巴西家庭都有一首不请自来的歌：在奶奶的生日会上，在桑巴圈的尾声，在只会四个和弦的叔叔的吉他上。在很多家里，这首歌就是《Carinhoso》。几乎人人听到开头几小节就认得出旋律；却很少有人知道，它曾在抽屉里被遗忘多年，因为作者本人觉得它拿不出手。
作者是小阿尔弗雷多·达罗沙·维安纳，人称皮欣吉尼亚，生于1897年4月23日，被许多人视为巴西流行音乐的伟大整理者。大约在1917年——确切日期研究者至今仍有争论——二十岁左右的他写了一首与众不同的肖罗。问题在于形式：这首曲子只有两个部分，而当时的肖罗应该有三个。几十年后，皮欣吉尼亚在里约图像与声音博物馆的口述访谈中说，正因如此他才把它收了起来。
当它终于离开抽屉，20世纪20年代有了一个器乐录音——但并非人人喜欢。《Phonoarte》杂志的评论家克鲁斯·科尔代罗认为前奏像狐步舞曲，甚至有人说皮欣吉尼亚“爵士化”了。今天看来颇具讽刺：当年显得太“洋”的东西，后来恰恰成了最巴西的象征。
转折出现在1936年。女歌手埃洛伊莎·埃莱娜要在里约热内卢市立剧院的一场慈善演出中唱一首新歌，便向朋友布拉吉尼亚（又名若昂·德巴罗）求助。他手头没有现成的作品，却主动提出为那段老旋律填词。据布拉吉尼亚本人说，歌词一个晚上就写好了——报酬是一条意大利领带。
1937年5月28日，当时最受欢迎的电台歌手之一奥兰多·席尔瓦在胜利唱片公司录下这首歌，《Carinhoso》成了那一年播放最多的歌曲。从那以后，它有了两百多个录音版本，从达尔娃·德奥利维拉、埃利泽特·卡多佐到埃利斯·雷吉娜、保利尼奥·达维奥拉和玛丽莎·蒙特；1950年甚至还有一个为电影制作的英文版。难怪很多人称它为“第二国歌”。
聆听时，请留意旋律——它起伏之间带着近乎说话般的细腻——还有两个部分之间的对比，正是当年让年轻作曲家觉得“太少”的那两个部分。布拉吉尼亚的歌词写的是一份温柔的爱：一颗只要看见心上人就欢喜的心。如果你需要一个再听一遍的理由，请记住：4月23日，皮欣吉尼亚的生日，是全国肖罗日。

items.grammar: Crase (à) is the preposition "a" fused with the article "a". "Prestar atenção" asks for "a", so "preste atenção à melodia" (a + a melodia), but "ao contraste" with a masculine noun. A quick test: if a masculine noun would need "ao", the feminine one needs "à". The same happens in the fixed expression "não é à toa".
items.grammar_zh: 重音符号 à（crase）是介词 “a” 与阴性冠词 “a” 的合写。“prestar atenção” 要求介词 “a”，所以写 “preste atenção à melodia”（a + a melodia），而阳性名词则是 “ao contraste”。小测试：如果换成阳性名词要用 “ao”，阴性名词就要用 “à”。固定说法 “não é à toa” 里也是如此。
